**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The IP and data ownership package in this agreement already sits at our preferred playbook position:

- **§14.1 — Customer Data and Customer IP:** We own all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material and independently developed IP. Vendor receives only a limited processing right, with no transfer of rights.
- **§14.2 — Deliverables:** Ownership vests in us on creation, backed by an express present assignment from Vendor, flow-down assignments from its personnel, and further-assurances. The "subject to payment of Fees" qualifier is market-standard and not a walk-away trigger.
- **§14.3 + §13.2 — Licence-back:** Vendor retains only pre-existing Vendor Technology, and anything embedded in a Deliverable carries a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence including modification, derivative works and contractor use — exceeding even the fallback standard.
- **§14.4 — No joint ownership:** Expressly negated absent a separate signed instrument; feedback is voluntary and we keep unrestricted rights in our own feedback.

I also verified the definitions do not quietly sweep our material into Vendor's column: "Vendor Technology" (§1.8) carves out Customer Data, our pre-existing IP, and anything embodying our Confidential Information, while "Customer Data" (§1.3) captures submitted material plus derived output, excluding only non-attributable anonymized telemetry. §15.1 reinforces this by barring sale, advertising use, cross-customer combination and model training without our written consent. Targeted searches for competing assignment, licence-to-Vendor, improvements or derivative-works grants elsewhere in the document returned nothing adverse.
